statements.impact_statement: Findings occur in .roady/state.json, an append-only project-management journal that records historical agent metadata. The file does not contain model-selection logic; it is audit bookkeeping. The model reference is not executed or loaded by the Chronos engine.

Finding is a false positive: internal/notify/webhook.go implements an HTTP webhook notifier (not an AI API). The Webhook type has its own best-effort retry logic on 5xx responses. The rule matched the 'retries' field name without understanding the domain context.

Finding is the literal string 'Bearer ' used as the RFC 6750 authorization scheme prefix in BearerAuth middleware. This is a protocol constant, not a secret token. The actual token is supplied via CHRONOS_API_TOKEN at runtime and compared with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare.

Findings are random UUIDs used as test fixtures (e.g. internal/pipeline/compute_test.go). They are generated with uuid.New() in test setup and have no production value. The rule's entropy heuristic cannot distinguish test data from secrets.

These containers exist only for the duration of a CI job, are not reachable from the internet, and use a trivial password acceptable for throwaway test data.

vulnerability.name: DATA-001
vulnerability.description: Email address in code or config

statements.impact_statement: .goreleaser.yaml contains the public package maintainer email (felix.geelhaar@gmail.com) required by Debian/RPM packaging conventions. This is intentionally public contact information, not a secret. internal/store/mysql/mysql_test.go contains a test-only email placeholder.

vulnerability.name: DATA-005
vulnerability.description: Hardcoded public IP address in configuration

statements.impact_statement: Finding in Dockerfile line 25 is the comment 'Bind 0.0.0.0 in containerised deployments via CHRONOS_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0'. 0.0.0.0 is a documented configuration hint for container networking, not a hardcoded production IP. The actual bind address is controlled by the CHRONOS_HTTP_HOST environment variable at runtime.

workflow_dispatch on .github/workflows/release.yml is intentional: it allows maintainers to trigger a release manually when automatic tag-push detection fails or when a hotfix must be built from a non-standard ref. The workflow requires write permissions and secrets that are only available to repository maintainers.

vulnerability.name: IAC-314
vulnerability.description: GHA workflow has contents write permission

statements.impact_statement: contents:write in .github/workflows/release.yml is required for goreleaser to create GitHub Releases and upload artefacts. The .goreleaser.yaml brews block also needs contents:write to push formula updates to the Homebrew tap repository. The workflow triggers only on tag push (v*) or manual dispatch by maintainers, limiting blast radius.

vulnerability.name: IAC-315
vulnerability.description: GHA workflow has packages write permission

statements.impact_statement: packages:write in .github/workflows/release.yml is required for goreleaser to push multi-arch Docker images to ghcr.io. The workflow triggers only on tag push (v*) or manual dispatch by maintainers. The ghcr.io registry is scoped to this repository.

These are security controls, not secrets.

vulnerability.name: IAC-013
vulnerability.description: GitHub Action pinned to mutable tag instead of commit SHA

statements.impact_statement: All flagged actions are pinned via dependabot from trusted publishers (actions/, github/, docker/, goreleaser/, golangci/). Each version bump generates a new line-content fingerprint that re-triggers this rule for the same low-actual-risk pattern. Dependabot keeps these up-to-date; the publisher allowlist effectively covers the supply-chain risk this rule targets at the project level.
